validated_properties: same resilient request replays exact prior response and next token without re-execution
expired in-progress request becomes UNCERTAIN and is never automatically re-executed
previous rolling token is client_request_id-bound for resilient requests
legacy clients without client_request_id remain on the original session-consume path
server request_id is never reused as the client idempotency key
nested parameter order canonicalizes recursively and nested secret fields are excluded from fingerprints
replay receipts contain no plaintext session id, old token or next token
session-open replay cannot roll a later token backward
deferred router guard preserves exact response status and lines
critical approval status is read-only and exact-binding-sha protected
pending update inspector requires a valid normal-session peek, does not rotate the session token, and hides internal package path
public source manifest status exposes hashes only, never source content
release consistency status is read-only and reports runtime/genome versus canonical memory without mutating either
rules: Do not promote files merely because they exist on the candidate branch.
Apply only against a live 0.9.15 source state whose hashes match LIVE_INTEGRATION_0.9.15.json, or re-read/rebase first.
Preserve the installed 0.9.15 workspace_proposal_batch route and proposal_ids contract.
UPDATE_PENDING_INSPECT is an authorized nonrotating session-peek diagnostic, not a public package metadata endpoint.
RELEASE_CONSISTENCY_STATUS is read-only; it must never auto-mutate canonical memory.
RED/production/kernel FreeOTP execution semantics must remain unchanged.
Authenticated mutation transport denial is not evidence that KiCom executed a request; never blind-retry an ambiguous mutation.
Synchronize canonical PROJECT_STATE/PROTOCOL/CHANGELOG/NEXT to 0.9.15 before release promotion or as an explicitly verified prerequisite.
All release promotion must pass isolated build validation, workspace-batch regression, genome/verifier checks and deliberate lost-response tests.
